verification_report.summary:
All three proposed extensions are correct under the stated standing setting and six accepted internal inputs. The audit completed 15 sequential statement checks and seven reference checks, with no critical errors or gaps.

For the divisorial proposition, the positive subsolution coefficient gives 0<c<=b<infinity, hence nonzero p in D_omega and 0<rho_omega(p)=b^(-1/n)<infinity. Smooth strictly positive tests have finite positive D_p. The divisor support is dV-null, so restriction of the positive trace-defect measure and Poincare–Lelong/Stokes give 0<=integral beta_E wedge T<=1-c^(1/n)D_p(T). Taking the smooth supremum proves 0<=kappa<1 and c<=b(1-kappa)^n. At c=b, every smooth maximizing sequence has pairing tending to zero; every cluster annihilates beta_E and kappa=0 excludes bigness. None of these conclusions uses uniform integrability. For E!=0, compactness, continuity, nonnegativity on the smooth-test closure, and strict positivity on its smooth members give the claimed nonempty proper exposed face of that closure.

Compactness supplies a convergent subsequence of the chosen smooth maximizing sequence. Maximization and uniform integrability pass to this subsequence, and the accepted selected-attainment criterion makes every such cluster maximize D_p. Both corollaries explicitly assume b>0, so their finite root-space membership and positive maximum are justified before applying that criterion. The standing nonzero-density hypothesis excludes the historical zero-density gap; b=0 is excluded, b=infinity is impossible here, and E=0 causes no invalid inference.

For the semipositive corollary, zero pairing forces tr(BP_T)=0 with respect to the full coefficient measure. Where B is nonzero, P_T is singular, so the determinant measure is supported on {beta_E=0}. Its absolute continuity and the f-null hypothesis imply p k_T=0 almost everywhere, contradicting the positive maximum. This does not assert vanishing of the trace current. If beta_E is identically zero, the f-null hypothesis is incompatible with nonzero f.

For the nef corollary, the maximizing annihilator exists as above. For each fixed smooth positive probability mu, positive lambda_mu(beta_E) would force its determinant measure to vanish and hence D_p(T)=0. Nef nonnegativity then gives lambda_mu(beta_E)=0. Smooth changes of Bott–Chern representative preserve the relevant pairings and volume. No interchange of density quantifiers or uniform lower-mass conclusion is used.

The old condition p in D_omega^0 supplies both b>0 and full-family uniform integrability, so the previous conclusions and Hopf illustration follow. The exceptional-curve example remains consistent with the face being confined to the smooth-test closure. No selected/global equivalence, unrestricted upper semicontinuity, approximation of all Gauduchon currents by smooth ones, singular product [E] wedge T, bigness/nef-volume identification, novelty, regularity, or exact equation is inferred. All cited dependencies are internal or expressly accepted; no external-paper reference requires arXiv/web search. Writes are confined to this verifier run; no manuscript, editorial, frozen-input, historical-result, or Git publication changes were made.
